pr_title: Make sure `MeshLibrary` shape array has correct number of elements
pr_body:
The shape array shown in the inspector increases and decreases by 2, ensuring that the last elements (when increasing) is a shape-transform pair.
Fixes: #53897

issue_context.title: Can't add element to the MeshLibrary Item Shapes array
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

3.3.stable

### System information

Archlinux

### Issue description

When trying to increase number of elements of the `MeshLibrary/Item[]/Shapes` array Godot fails with:
```scene/resources/mesh_library.cpp:262 - Condition "p_shapes.size() & 1" is true.```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3064914/137601620-104cc004-c30e-4253-b59b-e5c83f119c56.png)


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an empty `MeshLibrary`,
2. Add an item,
3. Increase the `Shapes` array size.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments:
Does it work if you write `2` or `4` as a size for the Shapes array? Given the error message[^1], it seems that only even numbers are allowed. I suppose the Shapes array expects *pairs* of shapes somehow.

[^1]: The binary operation `& 1` on an integer evaluates to `true` for odd numbers only. Since this is an error condition, it must evaluate to `false` for the operation to be considered successful.

@Calinou you are right, I hadn't checked it precise enough. I thought that when setting to some other number and pressing enter causes the same error, but it seems it just silently reverts to 0 in such case.
What the Shapes array expects is, for each shape, a Shape3D resource and its Transform (in that order). That's why it is expected to have an even number of elements.
My guess is that we should change the shapes size property to automatically round up the value to the nearest greater even number. For instance, if you specify 1, it will use 2 instead.
